app_summary: An online shop selling astronomy products, based on the OpenTelemetry Demo. It is built with polyglot microservices (Go, Java, .NET, Python, Node.js, Rust, ...) communicating via gRPC and HTTP behind an Envoy frontend-proxy, with Kafka for asynchronous order processing and Valkey as cart store. Supported Operations: View product catalog, Receive product recommendations and ads, Add item to cart, Checkout with selected items, Currency conversion, Process payment, Generate shipping quotes, Send order confirmation emails

final_report.root_cause: The payment service was unable to validate/authorize payment requests because the payment-gateway credentials/token-validation configuration (Kubernetes Secret) are missing from the astronomy-shop namespace and the payment Deployment/pod has no secret/env references for those credentials. As a result the payment app rejects all charge attempts with “Payment request failed. Invalid token.” and downstream checkout operations fail. The failure surfaced when the running payment container processed requests without any valid gateway credentials (either the secret was never provisioned or was removed/omitted during a deployment), so token validation always failed.
affected_resources: Service: checkout (checkout calls failed due to payment errors)
Traces/spans: multiple checkout->payment traces showing "Payment request failed. Invalid token."
Kubernetes Secret: payment gateway credentials (missing from astronomy-shop namespace)
final_report.evidence_summary: 1) Application traces (20+ error traces) and payment pod logs consistently show the error: "Payment request failed. Invalid token." (examples: traceIDs cce658c9ce21e6eb3fef0140824b5a66, fabc9f99ed50e38084ad3a5094f1f319). 2) kubectl inspection of the payment Deployment and pod (payment-6c5f448889-rgh86) shows the container environment contains only OpenTelemetry-related env vars and PAYMENT_PORT and contains no envFrom/secretKeyRef or volume mounts for credentials. 3) kubectl get secrets in the astronomy-shop namespace returns only grafana and the Helm release secret — there is no secret providing payment gateway credentials. 4) Service discovery is correct: checkout uses PAYMENT_ADDR=payment:8080 and the payment Service (port 8080) selects the payment pod, so connectivity/ports are not the issue. These correlated facts indicate functional authentication failure due to missing credentials rather than network, port, or pod lifecycle faults.
final_report.investigation_summary: Priority-1 investigation focused on the payment service credential/configuration epicenter. Actions: described payment Deployment and pod, fetched payment pod logs (tail), listed secrets in the astronomy-shop namespace, and attempted to reproduce/trace the error via traces. Priority-2 investigation verified checkout -> payment connectivity (checked checkout Deployment env PAYMENT_ADDR, payment Service ports/selector, and payment pod labels/ports). Findings show checkout resolves and connects to payment correctly, but payment is rejecting tokens because it has no configured credentials/secret. No evidence of pod crashes, restarts, port mismatches, or network connectivity issues was found. Based on the above, the investigation concluded the primary cause is missing/misconfigured payment gateway credentials (Kubernetes Secret) referenced by the payment service.
